title: Improving Diffusion Planners by Self-Supervised Action Gating with Energies
claim: A learned latent-consistency energy re-ranks sampled plans, gating value-based selection away from dynamically infeasible candidates without retraining the planner.
layout: 3 panels: two small top (a),(b), wide bottom (c) left-to-right; red infeasible path
description: A three-panel method diagram. Panel (a), top left, shows JEPA pretraining: a state window passes through Masking and an Encoder into context latents. An EMA teacher encodes a target state, a Predictor links the two, and a red L_JEPA loss compares them. Panel (b), top right, shows an action-conditioned predictor. A frozen encoder (snowflake icon) embeds s_t. Two branches, one with the true action a_t and one with a negative action a'_t, feed the predictor. The predictions are compared with the target latent through red L_tf + L_ro and L_neg losses. Panel (c), the wide bottom panel, is the test-time pipeline. A red Diffusion Planner fans out five blue candidate trajectories, and one wiggly red trajectory is marked infeasible. The candidates pass through the Encoder and Action Predictor, producing energy histograms. A gray Filter crosses out the red high-energy bar and selects the best-valued plan, shown in green, to output a_t. Color coding is teal for encoders, purple for predictors, red for failure and blue for feasible plans.
caption: The SAGE framework. (a) Learn a predictive JEPA state representation from masked state windows with an EMA teacher. (b) Train an action-conditioned latent predictor whose prediction error defines a transition energy. (c) At test time, score diffusion-generated candidate plans with this energy and gate value-based selection toward locally feasible actions
abstract: Diffusion planners are a strong approach for offline reinforcement learning, but they can fail when value-guided selection favours trajectories that score well yet are locally inconsistent with the environment dynamics, resulting in brittle execution. We propose Self-supervised Action Gating with Energies (SAGE), an inference-time re-ranking method that penalises dynamically inconsistent plans using a latent consistency signal. SAGE trains a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) encoder on offline state sequences and an action-conditioned latent predictor for short horizon transitions. At test time, SAGE assigns each sampled candidate an energy given by its latent prediction error and combines this feasibility score with value estimates to select actions. SAGE can integrate into existing diffusion planning pipelines that can sample trajectories and select actions via value scoring; it requires no environment rollouts and no policy re-training. Across locomotion, navigation, and manipulation benchmarks, SAGE improves the performance and robustness of diffusion planners.
